Print, summarize and tabulate an htna network comparison

Source: R/methods-comparison.R
htna_comparison-methods.Rd

print(), summary() and as.data.frame() read an htna_comparison object from compare_htna(), which describes how two heterogeneous transition networks differ edge by edge. Beyond the overall similarity and distance measures of the two weight matrices, the comparison splits the differences by actor-pair block: the transitions within each actor (for example Human to Human) and between actors (Human to AI, AI to Human). The actor-pair table shows where in the actor structure the two networks differ most.

print() shows the overall measures and the actor-pair table; for a grouped comparison it shows, for every cohort pair, the correlation and mean absolute difference of the edge weights and the actor-pair table. summary() returns the actor-pair table. as.data.frame() returns any of the comparison's tables, chosen with what; for a grouped comparison the tables of every pair are stacked with a leading comparison column.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'htna_comparison'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'htna_comparison'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'htna_comparison'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("actor_pairs", "edges", "metrics", "network")
)

# S3 method for class 'htna_comparison_group'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'htna_comparison_group'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'htna_comparison_group'
as.data.frame(
  x,
  row.names = NULL,
  optional = FALSE,
  ...,
  what = c("actor_pairs", "edges", "metrics", "network")
)

Arguments

x, object

An htna_comparison or htna_comparison_group from compare_htna().

...

Unused.

row.names, optional

Ignored; present for the generic.

what

Table to return: "actor_pairs" (default; one row per directed actor pair), "edges" (one row per edge of the aligned networks), "metrics" (one row per similarity or distance measure) or "network" (one row per network-level metric, with the values of both networks).

Value

print() returns x invisibly. summary() returns the actor-pair data frame. as.data.frame() returns a data frame:

  • "actor_pairs": source_actor, target_actor, n_cells, n_nonzero_x, n_nonzero_y, n_changed, mean_difference, mean_absolute_difference, rms_difference, max_absolute_difference; differences are x - y.

  • "edges": source, target, weight_x, weight_y, the difference measures of each edge, source_actor and target_actor.

  • "metrics": category, metric, value.

  • "network": metric, x, y.

For a grouped comparison every table has a first column comparison (for example "Early vs Late"), and the first-named cohort is x.

See also

compare_htna(), plot.htna_comparison_group()

Examples

data(human_ai)
grp <- build_htna(human_ai, actor_type = "actor_type", group = "phase")
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'cluster' (24 sessions), 'actor_type' (9 sessions)
#> Metadata aggregated per session: ties resolved by first occurrence in 'session_date' (1 sessions), 'cluster' (18 sessions), 'actor_type' (15 sessions)
comparison <- compare_htna(grp)
comparison
#> HTNA network comparisons: 1 cohort pair
#> 
#> --- Early vs Late ---
#>   Pearson correlation of edge weights: 0.959
#>   Mean absolute difference:            0.0192
#>  source target cells changed mean_diff mean_abs_diff max_abs_diff
#>   Human  Human    36      35   0.00168        0.0159       0.0631
#>   Human     AI    36      36  -0.00168        0.0179       0.0922
#>      AI  Human    36      36  -0.00622        0.0216       0.0571
#>      AI     AI    36      28   0.00622        0.0212       0.1810
summary(comparison)
#>      comparison source_actor target_actor n_cells n_nonzero_x n_nonzero_y
#> 1 Early vs Late        Human        Human      36          35          35
#> 2 Early vs Late        Human           AI      36          36          36
#> 3 Early vs Late           AI        Human      36          36          36
#> 4 Early vs Late           AI           AI      36          28          27
#>   n_changed mean_difference mean_absolute_difference rms_difference
#> 1        35     0.001681478               0.01593235     0.02279098
#> 2        36    -0.001681478               0.01791131     0.02767092
#> 3        36    -0.006221056               0.02158038     0.02683857
#> 4        28     0.006221056               0.02124805     0.04281287
#>   max_absolute_difference
#> 1              0.06311526
#> 2              0.09221141
#> 3              0.05710535
#> 4              0.18124427
as.data.frame(comparison, what = "metrics")
#>       comparison             category               metric       value
#> 1  Early vs Late    Weight Deviations      Mean Abs. Diff.  0.01916802
